name: Can I expand a bathroom and keep it accessible for aging in place?

mainEntity.name: How do I design a bathroom expansion so it works better for aging in place or mobility needs?
mainEntity.text: How do I design a bathroom expansion so it works better for aging in place or mobility needs?

acceptedAnswer.text: A bathroom expansion is one of the best times to design for aging in place or better mobility. Extra square footage can create wider turning space, easier shower access, and safer movement around the vanity and toilet. A curbless or low-threshold shower is often a strong choice because it reduces tripping risk and improves long-term usability. Blocking inside the walls should be added early if grab bars may be needed later. Better lighting, slip-resistant flooring, and a bench or built-in niche can also make the room more practical. If accessibility is a priority, the layout should be planned before framing starts so clearances are protected from the beginning. Even small design choices matter, such as door width, faucet style, and whether there is enough room for a future caregiver or mobility aid. A good accessibility-focused expansion can look luxurious while also being safer and easier to use over time.
acceptedAnswer.description: Yes, a bathroom expansion is a good chance to improve accessibility with wider clearances, a curbless shower, blocking for grab bars, better lighting, and non-slip flooring. These choices should be planned before framing and plumbing are finalized.
